title: Quality control, records and handover
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Avoiding unfair business practices (dated March 2016, per copyright page); NSW Government, Electrical licences and credentials (last updated 23 June 2026); NSW Government, Plumbing, draining and gasfitting (last updated 31 July 2026; page metadata shows a later modified date).
audience: Handyman workers and property maintenance workers who complete and hand over jobs
learningOutcomes: Check completed work against the signed scope and the product instructions.
Record defects, exclusions and referrals separately from completed work.
Hand over a job without implying that the whole property is safe or compliant.

instruction.heading: Check the work against the scope
instruction.body: Compare what was done with the signed scope, line by line. Check that each item was completed, that each product was used as the manufacturer instructions say, and that the finish is sound. Check the surfaces around the work for marks, and clear the area before you leave. A task that was agreed but not done is an exclusion, and it must be recorded as such. Do not record something as completed because it looks finished from the doorway.

instruction.heading: Record defects, exclusions and referrals separately
instruction.body: Keep three lists: completed work, exclusions (agreed but not done, or refused), and referrals (issues found during the work that need another trade). A referral is not a failure of the job; it shows the worker saw a risk and passed it on. Keep the lists separate so the client can see what is done and what remains. Photograph the finished work and any defect only with consent, and keep the images only for the job record.

instruction.heading: Handover without overclaiming
instruction.body: When you hand over, state what was done, what was not, and what needs referral. Never say that the property is safe or compliant unless a competent person has confirmed that. Under the Australian Consumer Law, statements that mislead or are likely to mislead are unlawful, and intent is not needed for a breach (ACCC guide, dated March 2016). A completed cabinet fix does not clear an unrelated electrical hazard found on the same visit. Obtain the client's sign-off on the completed items and the exclusion list, and keep a copy of the signed record with the work order.

procedure: Compare the completed work with the signed scope, item by item.
Check the products were used as the manufacturer instructions say, and record the products used.
Record completed items, exclusions and referrals in three separate lists.
Photograph the finished work and any defect, with consent.
Hand over to the client, stating what is done, what is not, and what needs referral.
Obtain the client's sign-off on the completed items and the exclusions, and file the record with the work order.

workedExamples.situation: A cabinet handle is fixed, but a damaged outlet seen during the visit remains unresolved.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the completion record and the handover describe the visit?
workedExamples.reasoning: Report the cabinet work as completed. Report the outlet as an urgent referral to a licensed electrical worker, recorded separately. Do not describe the property as safe, because the outlet is unresolved.

equipmentAndPpe: Signed work order and scope copy
Camera or phone for photos, used with consent
Product records or labels for the products used

commonErrors.error: Recording an agreed task as complete when it was only partly done.
commonErrors.prevention: Record partial tasks as exclusions with the reason.

commonErrors.error: Telling the client the whole property is safe after a small repair.
commonErrors.prevention: Report only what was checked, and list referrals separately.

commonErrors.error: Rewriting the record later to fit what was done.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the outcome on the day. Make any later correction as a dated addition.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A completion record does not confirm electrical, gas, plumbing or structural safety. The NSW wiring rule applies whatever the cost (electrical page, last updated 23 June 2026), and the NSW plumbing rule applies at any price (plumbing page, last updated 31 July 2026). The state positions are recorded in “Electrical boundaries and referral” and “Water, plumbing and gas boundaries”.
Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Every agreed item is marked as completed or as an exclusion with a reason.
Referrals are recorded separately from completed work.
The client signs off on the completed items and the exclusion list.
documentationEvidence: Completion checklist with completed items, exclusions and referrals
Photos of the finished work and any defect, with consent
Client sign-off on the completed record
summary: Check each item against the signed scope.
Keep completed work, exclusions and referrals in separate lists.
Never describe the property as safe or compliant unless a competent person has confirmed it.

knowledgeChecks.question: A task agreed in the scope was only partly done. How should it be recorded?
options: As completed, since most is done
Left off the record, so it is clean
As an exclusion with the reason
As completed, the rest done later

knowledgeChecks.question: An unrelated electrical hazard is seen during a cabinet repair. What should the handover say?
options: The property is safe overall, since the cabinet work is complete and nothing else is wrong
Nothing, because it is not in the scope of the cabinet job and was not requested by the client
The cabinet work is completed, and the electrical hazard is an urgent referral recorded separately
The electrical hazard is fixed if the client is happy with the cabinet work and the price

knowledgeChecks.question: When a record must be corrected after the job, how should it be done?
options: Rewrite the original entry so that it reads correctly
Delete the original and write a new one
Ask the client to forget the earlier entry
Make a dated addition that shows the correction
